correctness.rationale: For every rotation and translation, rotation-invariance of the Euclidean ball gives \(\rho(T+rB_2^d)+w=\rho T+w+rB_2^d\). By definition of erosion this is contained in a convex host \(K\) exactly when \(\rho T+w\subset K\ominus rB_2^d\). The eroded host is a nonempty compact convex set whenever the thickened host is Kakeya. Thus the parameter spaces of admissible thickened and unthickened placements are identical and every continuous path transfers both ways. Janzer's segment theorem plus similarity yields the capsule case. The width comparison correctly excludes both segments and balls for nondegenerate \(L\) and \(r>0\).

final_claim: Euclidean ball thickening preserves universal convex Kakeya rotatability: if \(T\) has the property then \(T+rB_2^d\) has it. Hence every nondegenerate capsule \(L+rB_2^d\) with \(r>0\) is universally rotatable and gives, for \(d\ge3\), a non-segment, non-ball answer to Janzer's Question 5.2.
limitations: The transfer requires a thickening body invariant under every rotation under consideration; an anisotropic fixed summand does not admit the same single erosion.
